what: ASML (Netherlands) makes the lithography machines that print circuits onto silicon wafers. It is the only company in the world that builds extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) machines, needed for the most advanced chips.
customers: Chipmakers such as TSMC, Samsung, Intel, SK Hynix and Micron.
money: EUV and DUV lithography machines costing up to several hundred million dollars each
service, upgrades and parts for machines already in factories
moat: A monopoly in EUV lithography built over decades with a unique supply chain (Zeiss optics, among others).
risks: Export limits on sales to China
Concentration on a handful of customers
opportunities: Revenue grew about 31% last year with a 35% operating margin
Return on invested capital of 39% and cash far exceeding debt
Analysts see about 49% upside, with high-numerical-aperture machines beginning to ship
watch: Bookings for EUV systems and guidance on 2027 and beyond.
